title: Nutritional vs X-Linked Hypophosphatemic Rickets: PHEX, FGF-23 and Burosumab
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology
module: Rickets, Calcium Disorders and Posterior Pituitary

steps.say: Nutritional cholecalciferol deficiency provokes secondary hyperparathyroidism and profound hypophosphatemia.
steps.tx: Evaluate baseline biochemical derangements by recognizing the classic **Nutritional rickets biochemical profile** on laboratory panels. Nutritional vitamin D deficiency rickets manifests with low or normal serum calcium, low serum phosphate, markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (> 500-1000 IU/L), elevated PTH, and serum 25(OH)D < 12 ng/mL (30 nmol/L).

vis.title: Nutritional Rickets Laboratory Findings
rows: Severe depletion of cutaneous and dietary cholecalciferol
Exaggerated unmineralized osteoid and osteoblast activity

steps.say: High dose oral cholecalciferol supplemented with elemental calcium rapidly promotes growth plate mineralization.
steps.tx: Restore total body stores through therapeutic repletion by administering **Stoss therapy high-dose vitamin D** with minerals. Treatment of nutritional rickets is oral cholecalciferol (vitamin D3 2000 IU/day for 12 weeks, or single-day stoss therapy 300,000-600,000 IU) along with elemental calcium carbonate supplementation (500 mg/day) to prevent hungry bone hypocalcemia.

vis.alt: Skeletal diagram and wrist radiograph demonstrating rachitic changes including distal metaphyseal fraying and widened physes.
vis.caption: Radiographic and skeletal manifestations of active pediatric rickets.

steps.say: Inactivating endopeptidase mutations lead to unregulated accumulation of circulating phosphaturic hormone.
steps.tx: Identify inherited renal phosphate wasting by investigating **X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets (XLH) genetics** in children. XLH is an X-linked dominant mutation in the PHEX gene (Xp22.1) causing loss of PHEX cleavage and pathological elevation of circulating Fibroblast Growth Factor 23 (FGF-23).

nodes.label: Failure of Physiological FGF-23 Endopeptidase Cleavage
Pathological Elevation of Circulating Intact FGF-23

steps.say: Elevated fibroblast growth factor suppresses proximal tubular phosphate transporters and blunts active vitamin D activation.
steps.tx: Delineate renal tubular transport failure by measuring **Tubular maximum phosphate reabsorption (TmP/GFR)** indices. FGF-23 downregulates apical sodium-phosphate cotransporters (NaPi-IIa / NaPi-IIc) in the proximal tubule, causing massive renal phosphate wasting with subnormal TmP/GFR and inappropriately normal/low 1,25(OH)2D levels. This defect manifests despite severe systemic hypophosphatemia.

vis.title: Renal Actions of Pathological FGF-23 Excess
rows: Accelerated catabolism of active vitamin D metabolites

steps.say: Targeted monoclonal antibody therapy neutralizes circulating hormone and corrects underlying phosphate homeostatic collapse.
steps.tx: Introduce targeted biologic therapy by prescribing the **Burosumab anti-FGF23 monoclonal antibody** in confirmed XLH cases. Burosumab (human anti-FGF23 IgG1 monoclonal antibody, 0.8 mg/kg SC every 2 weeks) normalizes renal phosphate reabsorption, heals rachitic bone lesions, and straightens lower extremity deformities superior to conventional therapy.

nodes.label: Direct Neutralization of Circulating Free FGF-23

steps.say: Frequent oral phosphate replacement alongside active metabolites risks severe renal calcification and gland hyperplasia.
steps.tx: Recognize adverse outcomes of legacy therapy reviewing **Conventional XLH therapy complications** during ongoing surveillance. Conventional therapy requires oral phosphate solutions (40-60 mg/kg/day divided 4-6 times daily) plus calcitriol (20-30 ng/kg/day); carries high risk of secondary/tertiary hyperparathyroidism and medullary nephrocalcinosis. Serial renal ultrasonography and urinary calcium monitoring are mandatory.

left.title: Oral Phosphate Solutions (40-60 mg/kg)
points: Divided into 4-6 doses daily around the clock

steps.say: Typical metaphyseal cupping, fraying, and growth plate widening indicate failure of provisional calcification.
steps.tx: Identify structural skeletal mineralization failure by examining **Radiographic hallmarks of active rickets** on skeletal surveys. Wrist and knee radiographs demonstrate cupping, fraying (brush-like appearance), widening, and splaying of the metaphysis with increased width of the radiolucent physis (growth plate). Cortical thinning and significant lower extremity bowing also occur.

vis.alt: Wrist radiograph of a child with rickets showing classic widening, cupping, and fraying of the distal radial and ulnar metaphyses.
vis.caption: Distal radial and ulnar metaphyseal cupping and fraying pathognomonic of rickets.

steps.say: Microscopic dental dentin defects permit rapid bacterial invasion and recurrent pulp necrosis.
steps.tx: Prevent recurrent orofacial complications by screening for **Dental abscesses in XLH** during regular dental examinations. Patients with XLH develop recurrent spontaneous periapical dental abscesses in non-carious teeth due to impaired dentin mineralization and enlarged pulp chambers, requiring proactive dental sealants.
